hypothesis: A breeding SiteID that has been abandoned requires a higher surrounding population state to be recolonized than the surrounding population state at which it was abandoned.

competing_predictions.reversible_static_site_quality: H approximately 0 for the same SiteID because occupancy maps reversibly onto population size after stable site quality is paired out.
competing_predictions.history_dependent_or_social_feedback: H > 0 because an empty site loses the state/social advantages of occupancy and recolonization requires greater surrounding population pressure.

abundance_definition.parent_state: leave-one-SiteID-out total abundance within the frozen species x MasterSite panel
abundance_definition.reason: excluding the focal SiteID prevents its own transition from mechanically entering the predictor
abundance_definition.transition_state: mean of log1p leave-one-site-out totals in the two years bracketing the transition

spell_estimand.interpretation: H>0 means spatial recovery requires a higher surrounding population state than spatial loss at the same SiteID
spell_estimand.measurement_boundary: A_e and A_c are annual transition-state proxies derived from the two censuses bracketing each occupancy transition; they are not exact continuous-time demographic thresholds.

aggregation.step1: average H across multiple completed spells within SiteID
aggregation.step2: average SiteID means within species x provider-resolved physical master_site_key
aggregation.step3: average physical MasterSite means within species
aggregation.step4: primary T = unweighted mean of species means

primary_inference.observed_statistic: T_obs = unweighted mean of species mean H after spell -> SiteID -> MasterSite -> species aggregation

species_sign_flip.null: species-level H means are symmetric around zero
species_sign_flip.test: one-sided sign-flip randomization of species means

structured_phase_null.purpose: Test whether positive H exceeds what can arise solely because fixed abandonment/recolonization dates align with a trending or autocorrelated surrounding-population trajectory.
conditioning: exact event-year pattern and vacancy duration
observed multivariate count trajectory within each species x MasterSite
maximal contiguous complete-year block containing each spell
shared provider-resolved physical master_site_key phase across species when the frozen contiguous block is identical
structured_phase_null.randomization: For each provider-resolved physical master_site_key x identical contiguous complete-year block, draw one common circular shift. Apply that same shift to every species, SiteID and spell sharing that MasterSite/block. Species with different frozen block boundaries are shifted separately. This preserves within-species cross-site covariance and, where blocks align, cross-species temporal covariance from shared local conditions. Keep frozen event-year positions fixed.
structured_phase_null.p_value: plus-one upper-tail probability that shifted species-balanced T >= T_obs
structured_phase_null.interpretation: A structured temporal-alignment null. It is not a fitted mechanistic occupancy model and does not remove time-varying habitat quality.

primary_inference.support: Require T_obs > 0, species sign-flip one-sided p <= 0.05, Delta_phase > 0, and structured-phase-null upper-tail p <= 0.05.

secondary_uncertainty.reporting: report species means, MasterSite means, SiteID means, all spell-level H values, and the structured phase-null summary

boundaries: Stage C is unauthorized unless the SiteID identity gate and provider-confirmed zero-semantics gate both passed before occupancy-state scanning.
A supported positive H is evidence that spatial recovery does not simply retrace spatial loss at the measured SiteID scale; it is not proof of an Allee mechanism.
Site pairing controls stable SiteID quality but not time-varying habitat degradation, predator change, disturbance or unmeasured management.
Do not call the result social hysteresis unless independent social-cue or fitness-density evidence is added.
Do not use first colonization events in the primary threshold comparison.
Do not change the completed-spell roster after count magnitudes are opened.
The structured phase null calibrates generic temporal alignment with observed parent-abundance trajectories and annual sampling but is not a complete reversible habitat-selection model.
Circular shifting creates a block seam; this is accepted as part of the frozen structured null and is not tuned after outcomes.
Use 'transition-state asymmetry' or 'empirical threshold proxy' in precise reporting; annual census data do not observe the exact continuous-time abandonment/recolonization threshold.

When multiple species share a MasterSite and identical phase block, the structured null uses one common phase shift to avoid treating shared local environmental trajectories as independent species evidence.
Physical phase blocks are keyed by provider-resolved master_site_key, not by display-name string alone.
MasterSite aggregation and phase blocking use provider-resolved physical master_site_key; display labels are retained only for presentation.
stop_rule: One execution only after the support gate passes. No alternative abundance transform, lag, transition midpoint, phase-block rule, circular-shift scheme, null family, site subset, minimum vacancy duration, species subset or weighting rule may be added after H is opened.
